reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches the refunds W2 reported. Starting by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches exactly what W2 reported: order 231 at 17910, 234 at 4004, and 235 at 1660. Next I need the list of orders so I know which customers to pay.

The refunds table matches W2's report exactly, so I can proceed. The orders cover three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each net balance from net_balance before recording any payout, starting with acme.
acme's net balance of 36083 matches its orders (18974 + 17109) with no refunds, so the figure checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 10785 matches its orders (21055 + 11644 = 32699) minus its refunds (17910 + 4004 = 21914). Next I'll get cobalt's net balance, the last customer in the batch.
Cobalt's net balance of 29267 matches its orders (14171 + 16756 = 30927) minus its refund on order 235 (1660). All three balances check out, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next is birch: its net balance of 10785 matches orders minus refunds, so I'll record that payout.
Cobalt's balance of 29267 checks out against orders minus the order 235 refund, and the refunds table matched W2's report. Recording cobalt's payout now completes the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully after the refunds table matched W2's report and each balance matched orders minus refunds. The batch is complete.
